Jerusalem the Instrument of Judgment on Her Foes Hereafter; Her Repentance and Restoration.</title> <div sID="gen24840" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13169"/><hi type="bold">1. burden--</hi>"weighty prophecy"; fraught with destruction to Israel's foes; the expression may also refer to the distresses of Israel implied as about to precede the deliverance.<div eID="gen24840" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24841" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">for Israel--</hi>concerning Israel [Maurer].<div eID="gen24841" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24842" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">stretcheth forth--</hi>present; now, not merely "hath stretched forth," as if God only created and then left the universe to itself (<reference osisRef="John.5.17">Joh 5:17</reference>). To remove all doubts of unbelief as to the possibility of Israel's deliverance, God prefaces the prediction by reminding us of His creative and sustaining power. entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 12 Zec 12:1-14 . Jerusalem the Instrument of Judgment on Her Foes Hereafter; Her Repentance and Restoration. 1. burden-- "weighty prophecy"; fraught with destruction to Israel's foes; the expression may also refer to the distresses of Israel implied as about to precede the deliverance. for Israel-- concerning Israel [Maurer]. stretcheth forth-- present; now, not merely "hath stretched forth," as if God only created and then left the universe to itself ( Joh 5:17 ). To remove all doubts of unbelief as to the possibility of Israel's deliverance, God prefaces the prediction by reminding us of His creative and sustaining power. Compare a similar preface in Is 42:5 ; 43:1 ; 65:17 , 18 . formeth ... spirit of man-- ( Nu 16:22 ; He 12:9 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13170"/><div sID="gen24844" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13170"/><hi type="bold">2. cup of trembling--</hi>a cup causing those who drink it to reel (from a Hebrew root "to reel"). Jerusalem, who drank the "cup of trembling" herself, shall be so to her foes (<reference osisRef="Isa.51.17">Is 51:17</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.51.22">22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.13.13">Jr 13:13</reference>). Calvin with the Septuagint translates, "threshold of destruction," on which they shall stumble and be crushed when they attempt to cross it. English Version is better.<div eID="gen24844" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24845" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">both against Judah--</hi>The Hebrew order of words is literally, "And also against Judah shall he (the foe) be in the siege against Jerusalem"; implying virtually that Judah, as it shares the invasion along with Jerusalem, so it shall, like the metropolis, prove a cup of trembling to the invaders. Maurer with Jerome translates, "Also upon Judah shall be (the cup of trembling); that is, some Jews forced by the foe shall join in the assault on Jerusalem, and shall share the overthrow with the besiegers. But <reference osisRef="Zech.12.6">Zec 12:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.12.7">7</reference> show that Judah escapes and proves the scourge of the foe. <div eID="gen24845" type="x-p"/>

Jerome states it was a custom in Palestine to test the strength of youths by their lifting up a massive stone; the phrase, "burden themselves with it," refers to this custom. Jerusalem--</hi>here distinguished as the country and the metropolis. Judah recognizes her "strength" to be "Jerusalem and its inhabitants" as the instrument, and "Jehovah of hosts their God" (dwelling especially there) as the author of all power (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.16">Joe 3:16</reference>). My strength is the inhabitants of Jerusalem, who have the Lord their God as their help. The repulse of the foe by the metropolis shall assure the Jews of the country that the same divine aid shall save them. <div eID="gen24852" type="x-p"/>

On "governors of Judah," see on <reference osisRef="Zech.9.7">Zec 9:7</reference>.<div eID="gen24853" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24854" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">hearth--</hi>or pan.<div eID="gen24854" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24855" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">torch ... in a sheaf--</hi>Though small, it shall consume the many foes around. Thus <reference osisRef="Isa.29.1-Isa.29.24">Is 29:1-24</reference>; <reference osisRef="Joel.3.1-Joel.3.21">Joe 3:1-21</reference>; Zec 12:<reference osisRef="1Cor.14.21">1-14:21</reference>, describe more Antichrist's army than himself. Daniel represents him as a horn growing out of the fourth beast or fourth kingdom; St. John, as a separate beast having an individual existence. Daniel dwells on his worldly conquests as a king; St. John, more on his spiritual tyranny, whence he adds a second beast, the false prophet coming in a semblance of spirituality. What is briefly described by one is more fully prophesied by the other [Roos]. <div eID="gen24855" type="x-p"/>

Jerusalem, however, also shall be specially strengthened against the foe.<div eID="gen24858" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24859" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">feeble ... shall be as David--</hi>to the Jew, the highest type of strength and glory on earth (<reference osisRef="2Sam.17.8">2Sa 17:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Sam.18.3">18:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Joel.3.10">Joe 3:10</reference>).<div eID="gen24859" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24860" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">angel of the Lord before them--</hi>the divine angel that went "before them" through the desert, the highest type of strength and glory in heaven (<reference osisRef="Exod.23.20">Ex 23:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Exod.32.34">32:34</reference>). "The house of David" is the "prince," and his family sprung from David (<reference osisRef="Ezek.45.7">Eze 45:7</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.45.9">9</reference>). David's house was then in a comparatively weak state. <div eID="gen24860" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv13178"/><div sID="gen24862" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv13178"/>10. Future conversion of the Jews is to flow from an extraordinary outpouring of the Holy Spirit (<reference osisRef="Jer.31.9">Jr 31:9</reference>, <reference osisRef="Jer.31.31-Jer.31.34">31-34</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.39.29">Eze 39:29</reference>).<div eID="gen24862" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24863" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">spirit of grace ... supplications--</hi>"spirit" is here not the spirit produced, but THE Holy Spirit producing a "gracious" disposition, and inclination for "supplications." Calvin explains "spirit of grace" as the grace of God itself (whereby He "pours" out His bowels of mercy), "conjoined with the sense of it in man's heart." The "spirit of supplications" is the mercury whose rise or fall is an unerring test of the state of the Church [Moore]. In Hebrew, "grace" and "supplications" are kindred terms; translate, therefore, "gracious supplications." The plural implies suppliant prayers "without ceasing." Herein not merely external help against the foe, as before, but internal grace is promised subsequently.<div eID="gen24863" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24864" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">look upon me--</hi>with profoundly earnest regard, as the Messiah whom they so long denied.<div eID="gen24864" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24865" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">pierced--</hi>implying Messiah's humanity: as "I will pour ... spirit" implies His divinity.<div eID="gen24865" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24866" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">look ... mourn--</hi>True repentance arises from the sight by faith of the crucified Saviour. It is the tear that drops from the eye of faith looking on Him. Terror only produces remorse. The true penitent weeps over his sins in love to Him who in love has suffered for them.<div eID="gen24866" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24867" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">me ... him--</hi>The change of person is due to Jehovah-Messiah speaking in His own person first, then the prophet speaking of Him. The Jews, to avoid the conclusion that He whom they have "pierced" is Jehovah-Messiah, who says, "I will pour out ... spirit," altered "me" into "him," and represent the "pierced" one to be Messiah Ben (son of) Joseph, who was to suffer in the battle with Cog, before Messiah Ben David should come to reign. But Hebrew, Chaldee, Syriac, and Arabic oppose this; and the ancient Jews interpreted it of Messiah. <reference osisRef="Ps.22.16">Psa 22:16</reference> also refers to His being "pierced." So <reference osisRef="John.19.37">Joh 19:37</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.1.7">Re 1:7</reference>. The actual piercing of His side was the culminating point of all their insulting treatment of Him. The act of the Roman soldier who pierced Him was their act (<reference osisRef="Matt.27.25">Mt 27:25</reference>), and is so accounted here in Zechariah. The Hebrew word is always used of a literal piercing (so <reference osisRef="Zech.13.3">Zec 13:3</reference>); not of a metaphorical piercing, "insulted," as Maurer and other Rationalists (from the Septuagint) represent.<div eID="gen24867" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen24868" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">as one mourneth for ... son--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Jer.6.26">Jr 6:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.8.10">Am 8:10</reference>). A proverbial phrase peculiarly forcible among the Jews, who felt childlessness as a curse and dishonor. Applied with peculiar propriety to mourning for Messiah, "the first-born among many brethren" (<reference osisRef="Rom.8.29">Ro 8:29</reference>). <div eID="gen24868" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 10. Herein not merely external help against the foe, as before, but internal grace is promised subsequently. look upon me-- with profoundly earnest regard, as the Messiah whom they so long denied. pierced-- implying Messiah's humanity: as "I will pour ... spirit" implies His divinity. look ... mourn-- True repentance arises from the sight by faith of the crucified Saviour. It is the tear that drops from the eye of faith looking on Him. Terror only produces remorse. But Hebrew, Chaldee, Syriac, and Arabic oppose this; and the ancient Jews interpreted it of Messiah. Psa 22:16 also refers to His being "pierced." So Joh 19:37 ; Re 1:7 . The actual piercing of His side was the culminating point of all their insulting treatment of Him. Future conversion of the Jews is to flow from an extraordinary outpouring of the Holy Spirit ( Jr 31:9 , 31-34 ; Eze 39:29 ). spirit of grace ... supplications-- "spirit" is here not the spirit produced, but THE Holy Spirit producing a "gracious" disposition, and inclination for "supplications." Calvin explains "spirit of grace" as the grace of God itself (whereby He "pours" out His bowels of mercy), "conjoined with the sense of it in man's heart." The "spirit of supplications" is the mercury whose rise or fall is an unerring test of the state of the Church [Moore]. In Hebrew, "grace" and "supplications" are kindred terms; translate, therefore, "gracious supplications." The plural implies suppliant prayers "without ceasing." Herein not merely external help against the foe, as before, but internal grace is promised subsequently. look upon me-- with profoundly earnest regard, as the Messiah whom they so long denied. pierced-- implying Messiah's humanity: as "I will pour ... spirit" implies His divinity. look ... mourn-- True repentance arises from the sight by faith of the crucified Saviour. It is the tear that drops from the eye of faith looking on Him. Terror only produces remorse. The true penitent weeps over his sins in love to Him who in love has suffered for them. me ... him-- The change of person is due to Jehovah-Messiah speaking in His own person first, then the prophet speaking of Him. The Jews, to avoid the conclusion that He whom they have "pierced" is Jehovah-Messiah, who says, "I will pour out ... spirit," altered "me" into "him," and represent the "pierced" one to be Messiah Ben (son of) Joseph, who was to suffer in the battle with Cog, before Messiah Ben David should come to reign. But Hebrew, Chaldee, Syriac, and Arabic oppose this; and the ancient Jews interpreted it of Messiah. Psa 22:16 also refers to His being "pierced." So Joh 19:37 ; Re 1:7 . The actual piercing of His side was the culminating point of all their insulting treatment of Him. The act of the Roman soldier who pierced Him was their act ( Mt 27:25 ), and is so accounted here in Zechariah. The Hebrew word is always used of a literal piercing (so Zec 13:3 ); not of a metaphorical piercing, "insulted," as Maurer and other Rationalists (from the Septuagint) represent. as one mourneth for ... son-- ( Jr 6:26 ; Am 8:10 ). A proverbial phrase peculiarly forcible among the Jews, who felt childlessness as a curse and dishonor. Applied with peculiar propriety to mourning for Messiah, "the first-born among many brethren" ( Ro 8:29 ).
